RL Data Atlas

From a candidate dataset to an Atlas source

Loading the catalog…

The RL Data Atlas lists every RL task source that Marin — the open training project whose job scheduler, dataset processing and app host this Atlas runs on — has declared, with its review state and evidence. A source is one pinned population of tasks, for example one Hugging Face dataset revision. A task is one RL problem stored as a TaskSpec: the prompt, the machine environment the agent works in, the answer contract and the grader (also called the verifier).

This page shows each path a dataset can take into the Atlas and what each outcome lets you rely on. Being listed is not the same as being approved for training: see the eligibility matrix, and the reader workflow for using an existing source. The counts come from the catalog snapshot that the Atlas currently serves, so they change when an operator loads a new snapshot. The normative rules live in the task curation reference; the steps below link to the maintained procedures. Synced to preview revision 30 (2026-11-18).

Current admission policy

Examples is the number of admitted tasks after filtration. There is no separate oracle column. Every header count is in tasks: admitted (TRAIN plus EVAL), pending oracle filtration, excluded, total population and tasks by quality. Shown follows filters and duplicate folding; the note accounts for hidden, filtered and folded tasks. Show everything clears filters, includes QUICK/BAD and expands every duplicate group. A source without an oracle shows its retained count minus typed static blockers. A source with an oracle shows Examples Pending until its current admission receipt exists.

  • License. Stage 0 is the first and binding check. The deterministic checker decides PASS, FAIL or ESCALATE at the dataset level; ESCALATE goes to the user. Agents never interpret licenses by hand or trace lineage themselves. Doubt means ban, and bans stay binding in the decision registry until the user records a lift on new primary evidence. Our own repackaged containers carry their upstream's license, and Marin's own datasets are released under OpenMDW 1.1. Published cards state the checker-verified license identifier, lowercased (apache-2.0, cc0-1.0), and per-folder receipts bind the resolved upstream pin. A third-party repackager that collects other projects' data is checked per folder against each folder's original upstream; a repackager's own empty or missing card is never a ban for the whole dataset. A dataset whose tasks are each built from its own upstream repository is checked per task against that repository's license, and only tasks whose repository passes the accepted list are kept.
  • Private data tier. Every source declares a typed restriction — open or private_always — set explicitly in code, orthogonal to license, Use and status. A private_always source's task text, prompts, answers, examples, curriculum samples, review excerpts, rollout transcripts and difficulty trajectories never leave its private store: the app shows counts, statuses, hashes and receipts, with the marker Private data: content is not displayed. wherever content would appear. Publication helpers refuse a private source; derived artifacts inherit the tag and a downgrade or missing tag is refused; audit sampling is refused. A versioned registry of user rulings can force a source private regardless of what a stored declaration says.
  • Sources with oracles. The original oracle solution runs on every task through the production Harbor trial path. Tasks whose oracle fails are dropped before ingestion. When the grader reads the agent's workspace, a nop agent that does nothing must also fail: a task is admitted only if its oracle passes and its nop does not. A nop pass excludes the task as NEGATIVE_CONTROL_PASSED. A nop run killed by a signal or an interrupted producer gets one re-drive at the same budget. A 600-second verifier deadline or a source error on the unsolved state counts as not passing. Tasks graded only on their answer need no nop control.
  • Sources without oracles. Examples is the count retained after deduplication and lexical decontamination, minus tasks with a typed static blocker such as tool_provider_required. No per-task execution proof is required for now.
  • EVAL sources are admitted to Atlas as evaluation data after applicable filtration, and remain excluded from TRAIN selection. Deduplication and lexical measurement still apply; EVAL overlap is not remediated.
  • Non-agentic tasks have no actor, harness or workspace: the model answers and the grader checks the answer. They skip every check that only makes sense for an agent: resource and timeout specs, calibration, package locks, Docker bases and image builds, tool providers, shared executors, backend fit, network policy and nop controls. A grader verdict, oracle filtering where an oracle exists, content QA, deduplication, decontamination, cross-source overlap and the EVAL rules still apply. This is decided per task from its TaskSpec, never by source name.
  • Agentic tasks run in exactly their own environment; a substitute image needs a mechanical no-op proof and a new dataset version. Declared limits are kept. Missing limits are calibrated from 1 CPU, 2 GiB memory, 2 GiB disk, a 300-second agent timeout and a 60-second verifier timeout, doubling only the limit that failed. The whole task contract must run on a production backend, with each task's declared network policy.
  • Execution backends. Sources that need a real root executor run on Daytona EVAL with explicit declarative provisioning built from the package Dockerfile — no named snapshots — capped by the account's measured capacity (64 concurrent sandboxes). Baked images are not published.
  • Backend survey. Each backend cell is SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED or VERIFY. PARTIAL means the backend runs the population with a named capability only partly met, such as non_root_user; it counts as runnable for admission, and Backends shows it as its own state with the capability and per-role counts. VERIFY means only a live run can show the capability, such as memory, CPU, disk or network enforcement; a live probe job at the source's exact declared profile resolves it to SUPPORTED or UNSUPPORTED. UNSUPPORTED is reserved for a capability the backend's code demonstrably lacks. A new admission waits for its VERIFY cells; an Available source stays Available with a verification-pending marker. Development-only backends, such as local docker-gvisor, have their own visual style and never count toward admission.
  • Admission checks. Before a source shows Available, every declared environment artifact must exist in a storage region, and at least one surveyed backend must be able to run the population; a source whose tasks declare no machine roles at all is exempt. A cohort no backend can run is Excluded with NO_SUPPORTED_BACKEND. Difficulty never excludes a source by itself: it records typed evidence, and a source-owned condition escalates through the admission procedure.
  • Re-pins. A re-pin requires a fresh census at the new pin even when the task count matches: a new revision can change content. A census receipt that its own evidence contradicts is refused, and content-changed sources need fresh deduplication, lexical measurement and a SAMPLE panel drawn on the current pin before their status is current. An archived-lineage panel cannot qualify a new admission.
  • Releases. Remediation publishes one new private open-athena pinned version per source. Prepared images go in a new GHCR package per source with internal visibility, never public. Every puller needs a read credential: the Iris clusters rno2a, 02a and 08a, and the Daytona RL and EVAL organizations. The survey probes the internal-image pull live, and a backend that cannot pull is UNSUPPORTED for internal-image sources. Artifacts are never deleted; changes get a new version.
  • Overlap and contamination. Exact duplicate contracts are dropped in every source. Lexical 13-gram overlap is removed from TRAIN sources and only measured for EVAL sources. Cross-source overlap matches each task to its most similar task in the other source, never by task ID, and a model cannot downgrade a measured overlap. A new Available admission must declare its Use explicitly: TRAIN needs a decontaminated private-release receipt at its pin, and EVAL needs a measured benchmark receipt at its pin.
  • Quality. Result is GOOD when at least 90% of reviewed tasks are clean, BAD when at least 50% have issues, and SOME_ISSUES otherwise. QC never rejects a task or a source by itself: a BAD-quality source can be admitted with its weakness documented (the Terminal-Pivot precedent). A grader content-quality finding, such as LaTeX-wrapped expected-answer strings recorded on a math source, is a typed finding on the source; the grader stays unchanged, and a private remediated version is optional data repair that needs its own SAMPLE QA and admission. A FULL review can be finalized with at most 1% of tasks unreviewed under a pinned waiver. Judges run at temperature 0.7 through the production judge service. QUICK sources can be admitted but are hidden by default; Show everything reveals them.
  • Counts. Only Available sources contribute admitted tasks. Pending, Excluded and Deprecated sources contribute zero admitted tasks, and Pending tasks are never in the admitted total.
  • Jobs. Curation jobs use three-day timeouts and run in the data's region. Infrastructure failures are re-driven and never count as task failures.

The paths

Solid edges are the path a candidate takes; dashed edges leave it for an outcome or an alternate route. Agentic tasks need a machine (a shell, files or tools). Non-agentic tasks skip machine provisioning and every other agent-only check; every source still needs a grading-boundary assessment. Select an outcome to list its sources.

the candidate's required path exit into an outcome, or an alternate route such as the non-agentic bypass

Read the evidence before selecting data

In the preview, sources awaiting an exact-input SAMPLE Result display QUICK. Their Quality tooltip and Evidence say “SAMPLE review in progress”; Result and issue rate stay unmeasured. The source declaration and execution evidence remain unchanged.

Hover over a Quality chip or open a source’s Evidence page to see the recorded reason its level is below FULL. The page links review receipts and shows the SAMPLE tasks reviewed, tasks selected and retained population. It identifies a FULL review for a different dataset version, converter version or task population, or the number reviewed in an incomplete FULL review. “No recorded FULL review” means no linked record was found; it does not say whether a review was scheduled or deliberately omitted.

Quality levels define the required content-review scope: QUICK converts without content review, SAMPLE requires at least 95% conclusive reviews of its fixed selected sample, and FULL requires review of the whole retained population, or an explicitly accepted whole-source waiver accounting for every unreviewed task and exact reason. An accepted waiver gives a final Result while Evidence still shows false strict coverage and the missing-review count. A provisional Result marks an unfinished required review, including unreviewed or uncertain tasks. Execution qualification is separate: content review does not prove that tasks execute successfully. QUICK is enough for admission, but the default view hides QUICK sources; Show everything lists them, and training uses one only when it is selected explicitly.

Use comes from the registered converter’s explicit TRAIN or EVAL policy. A benchmark tag never overrides TRAIN. Historical declarations without recorded Use display Unknown; a new admission without an explicit Use is refused.

Task review browsing. A FULL or SAMPLE quality chip opens that source's per-task review list, with paging and filters by verdict, confidence, reference status and defect. Each task review then opens the raw reviewer input, output and provenance behind the stored judgment. Reviews joined from original reviewer batches carry archived lineage: the original reviewer identity is shown as archived evidence, never as current-pin QA, and ambiguous or missing mappings stay explicitly not mapped with reasons. The six typed defect definitions are listed on the QC defect types page. When a release's review rows are not loaded, a visible banner says so and no per-task links appear.

Difficulty. The Difficulty tab shows coverage computed in code at each build: MEASURED, NEEDS_MEASUREMENT and BLOCKED counts per source and per solver. A Difficulty cell in the main table opens that measurement's attempts browser directly. The attempts browser lists a measurement's recorded attempt records and opens each rollout: its transcript and tool calls, model input, verifier output, and hashed Filer links to the raw attempt receipt and rollout archive. Difficulty is typed evidence only; it never excludes a source.

Result is computed from conclusive content reviews: GOOD means at most 10% with issues, BAD means at least 50%, and SOME_ISSUES lies between. Uncertain and unavailable observations stay explicit. QC never rejects tasks or sources. Mechanical conversion, environment, oracle and contamination exclusions have their own ledgers. A missing Result is unassessed, not a clean result.

Some issues · provisional A FULL Result is provisional when its required review is incomplete, including unreviewed or uncertain observations, unless a pinned whole-source waiver explicitly finalizes it. A SAMPLE panel with at most 5% missing observations has a final Result for its sample. Above 5% it stays provisional. The seed and panel stay fixed, without replacement or resampling. Missing IDs, reasons, bounded attempts and hashed deployment/batch receipts remain recorded; reviewed/unavailable counts and strict coverage stay truthful. The accepted_incomplete waiver applies only to FULL. The Issue rate column shows the conclusive issue fraction; review progress and lower bounds are on the source Evidence page. Enum chips carry their whole label with no text beneath them. The Overlap column counts flagged tasks in the measured input.

Contamination

Contamination records lexical overlap with the evaluation corpus. Counts refer to the measured input population, before duplicate and lexical exclusions. This measurement does not establish semantic decontamination.

NO ISSUES
A zero-overlap measurement binds to the current input pin or a validated current retained-release receipt.
REMEDIATED
TRAIN overlap was found and excluded in a new pinned private TaskCompendium release. Its validated remediation receipt must match the current dataset pin.
MEASURED, EVAL
Overlap was measured for a source declared EVAL and retained by policy. Inspect the overlapping-task count and matched evaluations in Evidence.
REMEDIATION REQUIRED
TRAIN overlap is measured but the current private pin lacks verified remediation. This state violates ingestion requirements and requires attention before training selection.
NOT MEASURED
No applicable current-pin lexical record exists. Historical evidence can remain available; the current source has no cleanliness claim.

The outcome lists below group sources by recorded execution oversight and source status, independently of Quality. A source with FULL content review can still have execution qualification pending. Open a source for its exact pin, counts and evidence.

Recorded execution and source status
CategoryWhat it recordsSources
Grandfathered blendA frozen historical exception; missing environment measurements remain unavailable. It does not establish new QA.

Open Backends for the Daytona actor verdict, unique snapshot count against the cap, failed requirements, measurement provenance and the operations link. The main-table Backends tooltip carries the same evidence.

Drag a source-table header edge to resize a column. Keyboard users can focus its separator and use arrow keys, Home or End. Widths persist per viewer; Reset column widths restores automatic sizing.

In Curriculum, every task is placed at its nearest subject and capability. The Confidence menu filters placements by similarity: All (nearest, the default), Broad, Moderate, Strict and the original cutoffs. Below a level's subject cutoff a task counts as Unplaced; a task that passes only the subject cutoff counts under “Other/unlisted (subject only)”. Every area includes empty capabilities. Sampled examples are pooled across sources, each labelled with its Source; filtering by source is optional. Sort areas by name or task count. Confidence levels are similarity filters, not calibrated probabilities.

A source's Evidence page can show a filtered private release pending qualification: its oracle filtering is complete, but the final release has not yet passed its own census, deduplication, contamination, grading and SAMPLE checks. Those tasks are not admitted or selectable until it does.

Once that final release passes, its own qualification, SAMPLE and oracle-admitted receipts admit it. Revision 19 admitted the first such releases: 9 QA and 14 Code filtered private releases. A candidate can also show its SAMPLE receipt on its parent source’s Evidence page before it is admitted; those tasks stay pending.

Grader and the oversight level are derived from each source's final TaskSpecs and QA records, never hand-declared. Evidence shows one oversight level, identical to the table's Quality, with a link to the receipt it comes from.

SAFE
Measured actor requirements fit the recorded Daytona capability and the ten-snapshot identity budget. Grouped images share one identity only when their declared CPU, memory and storage match; distinct profiles count as separate identities. Provisioning, quota headroom and completed rollouts are not established.
UNSAFE: reason
Recorded actor requirements exceed a limit or use an unsupported capability. The source remains listed.
N/A or pending
N/A requires a complete census with zero actor machines. Missing measurements remain pending. Grading machines do not enter the actor's Daytona label.

The required ingest order

1 Declare an immutable input

Every source has a registered converter, a canonical ID, an immutable dataset pin and upstream provenance. Historical IDs resolve through the alias table. Register the source through all_sources(); inventory-only declarations are not current runnable sources. See Declarations.

2 Preserve the task contract

New agentic sources ingest TaskCompendium or Harbor task directories. Internal MarinSkyRL format is accepted only for the frozen grandfather list. Prompts, answer contracts, environments and graders belong to the task specification.

3 Assess environment fidelity and grading boundaries

Tasks run in exactly their specified environment. A shared image cannot replace it. A repaired release completely describes its runtime behavior; ingestion-time transformations require SAMPLE or FULL QA and a new pinned version.

Every conversion assesses SHARED versus SEPARATE grading on every task. Workspace state and repository capabilities require SHARED execution; independent submitted-program or typed file-only contracts may use SEPARATE grading. A mismatched boundary is a mechanical rejection. Source-level declarations do not override task requirements. Inspect the per-source census and evidence. See Environments.

4 Convert, deduplicate and decontaminate

The mandatory order is conversion, exact within-source deduplication, lexical decontamination, resource calibration (agentic tasks only) and full-population oracle filtering, then SAMPLE/FULL QA. Raw, unique and dropped counts must reconcile, with a manifest explaining each exclusion.

Lexical measurements bind to the exact dataset revision. TRAIN remediation removes the union of duplicate and lexical exclusions; EVAL sources remove duplicates and retain lexical flags without lexical exclusions. Remediation produces a new private open-athena TaskCompendium release. QA and execution evidence bind to that retained population. Cross-source duplicate/subset display groups are distinct from within-source drops and do not authorize deleting data. They pair each task with its nearest neighbor in the other source, never by task ID; a model cannot downgrade a measured overlap.

QUICK converts without review. SAMPLE uses a bounded QA panel; FULL processes the complete population; complete content review requires its own coverage evidence. Processing mode, execution oversight, content Quality and Result are separate fields. See Within-source deduplication and Lexical decontamination.

5 Filter oracles and qualify execution

Oracle filtering covers every oracle-bearing task in both SAMPLE and FULL. A sampled control pass rate never exempts unsampled oracle-bearing tasks. The retained cohort is the passing subset; infrastructure errors are re-driven and never count as oracle failures. Workspace-graded tasks also need a full-population nop negative control that does not pass. Content QC remains informational and never rejects tasks.

The Filtration column shows EXCLUDED and Examples 0 for a complete, current-pin private filtration output with no retained tasks. This is a mechanical exclusion, not an admission or execution claim. Oracle-bearing sources show Pending oracle filtration until final evidence is bound. No-oracle Examples equal the current retained count minus unique typed static blockers under the pinned policy ruling; EVAL tasks enter total Atlas admission as evaluation data and remain excluded from TRAIN selection. Actorless answer-only tasks are exempt from agentic-only environment, lock, tool, network and workspace checks under their pinned ruling. Grading, content QA, deduplication, lexical checks and original-oracle filtering still apply. Missing static measurements remain unmeasured. The ledger links canonical filter, private output and validation receipts with their SHA-256 hashes. Content QA and backend fit never supply an admitted count.

Sources without oracle solutions

No per-task execution proof is required for now; the requirement can be restored later. Examples counts the tasks retained after deduplication and lexical decontamination, minus tasks with typed static blockers such as tool_provider_required or shared_executor_required. Content QA, environment fidelity, deduplication and decontamination still apply. Payload preservation, setup execution and verifier liveness checks remain available as diagnostics; a rebuilt environment uses them to show its spec is faithful. See Sources without oracle solutions.

LLM-judged sources

The implemented JUDGE_TIERS table defines LIGHT, MEDIUM and HEAVY judge specifications. Choose a tier after reviewing ten frozen tasks by hand and record the rationale. Pin the model identity and available revision, rubric, inputs, context and completion budgets, reasoning, temperature (0.7), parsing and retry settings. Endpoint configuration stays separate from the task's judge contract.

A pinned preset establishes a contract; source qualification remains pending until end-to-end controls and review demonstrate its behavior through the production grader. Record unavailable immutable weight identities as limitations. The curation reviewer uses its own pinned ReviewerSpec, separate from the task's reward judge. See LLM-judged sources and Oracle filtering.

6 Read actor capacity separately

Daytona labels measure actor machines only. Grading runs according to each task's SHARED/SEPARATE contract and does not change the actor label. A static census does not prove live quota, image availability or successful execution. Per-source backend fit remains unassessed when no current complete task-spec census was loaded.

7 Publish evidence, then load the intended app

Dataset publication, catalog publication, application code release and catalog loading are separate operations. Repaired and converted datasets are private open-athena TaskCompendium releases with immutable pins and provenance, one new version per source. Prepared task images use a new internal GHCR package per source. Inspect campaign outcomes before selecting a catalog snapshot. Loading a complete snapshot selects it atomically; failed staging preserves the serving selection.

This preview does not authorize production publication. Follow the Atlas preview procedure with the explicit preview app ID. Production remains on hold.

After admission: training selection

Only TRAIN sources with eligible FULL-mode artifacts may supply a training population. EVAL sources stay evaluation-only. A selection recipe names sources and quotas and pins the heldout set. Its exact heldout matching and cross-source deduplication supplement mandatory version-bound lexical decontamination; they do not replace it or establish semantic decontamination.

Before a training run

License is stage 0, before conversion or QA. The deterministic checker uses the pinned dataset’s own card, LICENSE files and README license statements: PASS permits ingest, FAIL stops it, and ESCALATE requires a user decision. Agents do not trace lineage or interpret uncertain terms themselves. Active bans remain binding until the user records a lift in the decision registry. See the stage-0 procedure.

  1. Verify the retained dataset pin, intended Use, license and private access.
  2. Read raw/unique/drop counts, lexical remediation and their manifests.
  3. Inspect content Quality, Result and provisional coverage separately from execution qualification.
  4. Check full-population oracle evidence, the SHARED/SEPARATE grading census and backend requirements.
  5. Use the current selection procedure and quick RL loop; Atlas visibility alone does not establish eligibility.

Use or add a source

Read the current catalog

A source folds under a larger source only when measured directional containment is at least 95%. Equal-size sources prefer FULL, then SAMPLE, then QUICK Quality, then source ID. Partial overlap stays in Evidence/detail views with qualified source names, measurements in both directions and evidence links; partial edges never chain into a folded group.

Source cells show only the source name and optional fold toggle. Origin/build information, dataset links and overlap notes are on Evidence/detail views. Backend fit preserves Supported, Partial and Unsupported survey states. Partial names its conditional capabilities and affected-task counts. Partial on a production backend can satisfy the backend admission gate; other admission checks still apply. N/A means the role does not exist. Agent and grader counts can overlap; do not add them into a unique-task total.

The source table hides QUICK, BAD, Excluded and Pending rows and folds measured duplicate/subset groups by default. One Status-filter click brings Excluded or Pending rows back, and Show everything clears every filter. Source evidence links always open the selected source, including entries hidden by table defaults. Missing measurements show as unavailable, never as zero.

Curriculum coverage selects the current live-source release and keeps the previous retained 59-source release selectable. Older pre-remediation and archived all-source artifacts remain historical evidence through their SHA-bound provenance receipts. Coverage applies only to the sources in the selected release. Approved role corrections show effective Use and preserve sampled evidence's historical role, with a receipt link. Coverage does not establish training eligibility.

Add a source using the maintained procedure

Use Adding a dataset and the task curation reference for current commands, immutable inputs, reviewer configuration and qualification gates. Preserve each attempt's evidence and publish a new version when a task contract changes. A local conversion check does not establish admission or complete QA.

Follow the recorded evidence

Each source page links its pinned current release, upstream input, duplicate/drop manifests, lexical measurements, grading assessment and available QC or execution receipts. Storage pointers include Filer links. Private files require the corresponding Marina or dataset access. A missing field or inaccessible artifact remains an explicit limitation.

Source status and exclusions

The four statuses

Every source carries exactly one status. Pending covers every source queued in the intake list that is not configured for the catalog yet, and every configured source whose only exclusion claim is a missing lexical remediation receipt; each Pending row records its current stage (Intake queued, Measurements pending, Admission pending or Lexical remediation queued) and a remediation agent produces the missing receipt. Available sources pass every admission check at their current pin. Excluded covers every source that cannot or may not be selected: the former Not-selectable state and every policy exclusion fold into it, and a row whose lexical remediation claim comes with any other exclusion reason stays Excluded. Deprecated means trainable but no longer supported or recommended; selection may use a Deprecated source when explicitly asked, never by default, and a Deprecated row carries no exclusion reason. A deprecated-tagged source with any exclusion reason is Excluded instead, and its replacement is shown when one exists.

Excluded requires a reason and evidence

An Excluded source always carries at least one typed exclusion reason with evidence: a receipt URI (with its SHA-256 where pinned), the failing check's output, an issue link for bans, or the missing artifact the failing stage expected. Exclusion without a claim is a construction error, never a display state. The reasons enumerate every exclusion path: license bans and missing licenses, zero-retained oracle filtration, missing or stale actor censuses, empty retained populations, incomplete grading censuses, missing graders, missing lexical receipts or required remediation, missing oversight, missing agentic task formats, missing snapshot-identity or execution measurements, declared environment artifacts that exist in no storage region, populations no surveyed backend can run, unqualified judge routes, invalid references, eval-only benchmark rulings, contamination risk, superseded populations, grader defects, duplicates, snapshot-budget limits, non-task-data upstreams, and a transitional needs-ruling state that the user must resolve.

What clears an exclusion

A source becomes Available only when every reason is cleared by evidence, never by hand. Each reason names its clearing step: census reasons clear with a census receipt at the current pin, grading reasons with a complete grading census, lexical receipt reasons with a measured receipt at the pin, and the lexical remediation reason clears when a remediation agent publishes the clean or remediated private-release receipt at the current pin — the row queues as Pending with the stage Lexical remediation queued until then. Task-format and measurement reasons clear with the missing measurement. Environment-artifact reasons clear by rebuilding the artifact in region and binding its receipt; a backend reason clears with a survey recording a runnable backend at the current pin; the judge reason clears by re-pinning to a served tier in a remediation version; the invalid-reference reason clears with a faithful repair whose references resolve. License or policy reasons clear with the recorded user ruling and its registry update. The full per-reason table lives in the task curation reference.

Reading the status page

The status page lists every source — catalog rows, the pending intake queue and declaration-only metadata rows for known-but-rejected upstreams — with filters by status and reason, counts per status, and the list of sources whose exclusion still needs a ruling. Reason labels open their canonical one-line meaning and their clearing step; that explanation appears only when clicked, and the page itself shows data, never policy prose.

Repair candidates

What a repair candidate is

A repair candidate is a "cleaned subset" of a source the Atlas already tracks, offered by a third party (for example a validated-tasks folder against its TaskTrove counterpart). The repair lane never deprecates or excludes the tracked source and never admits the candidate as a parallel source: matched candidate tasks replace their tracked counterparts task by task, and only after passing every gate. Matching is content-only — task IDs are display labels, never matching keys.

The match classes

Every candidate is content-matched against the tracked population: identical (hash-proven same task, nothing to review), repaired (each side is the other's unique best neighbor at similarity ≥ 0.5 after the approved template stripping, and enters comparative review), new (no counterpart at or above 0.5, follows normal admission), or conflicting (a non-mutual nearest neighbor, or several candidates claiming one tracked task — a manual ruling is required and nothing is replaced by itself). Tracked tasks the candidate leaves out become advisory dropped-by-candidate flags on their QC evidence; the candidate's own filter is a signal, never an exclusion by itself. A candidate with zero overlap is a parallel derivation, not a cleaned subset — its advisories are suppressed and the folder is reported for a separate ruling.

How replacement is decided

Each repaired pair runs one comparative judge call (the pinned FULL-QC GLM-5.3 reviewer at temperature 0.7) under the atlas-repair-comparative rubric, returning better / tie / worse / incomparable plus exactly which defects the candidate fixes and which it introduces. A candidate replaces the original only when the comparison is not worse, it introduces no defects, and its own oracle and nop negative control pass. Every failed gate is recorded as typed evidence, and the original is kept otherwise.

Reading the provenance

The lane publishes a new private version of the tracked source with per-task provenance — original, replaced, or added — alongside the replaced task's hash and the advisory drop flags. The assessment page and each task's Evidence page carry those provenance fields and the comparative verdict receipts behind them. The source itself keeps its Available status and carries no exclusion reason; the candidate never appears as its own row.

Curriculum confidence and examples

Confidence selects precomputed subject and capability similarity cutoffs. All (nearest) is the default. Counts and stored sample examples update together; examples show their Source without requiring a source selection. Complete per-source counts are available below the samples. Lists are samples, not a complete instance index.

Grader profiles

Grader is derived from measured task contracts. Mixed uses one chip with its breakdown and judge profile in Evidence. A changed or unmeasured input stays Pending.
